slug: 2025-01-01 Sierra Leone Government Service Bus prototype - Terms of Reference (World Bank)

facts.fact: The World Bank's terms of reference say a Japan QII grant signed on 26 April 2025 funds a Government Service Bus prototype on an open-source platform such as X-Road, hosted in the Ministry of Finance data centre, to link PFM systems including IFMIS, ITAS, ASYCUDA and CRVS.
The terms of reference say there is no government service bus with agreed protocols within the PFM ecosystem and the systems operate standalone (date is the document's published year).

The Ministry of Finance's 20 May 2026 expression-of-interest notice requires the rollout firm to ensure data exchange between MOPTAX and CGMRS and integration with the Government Service Bus, and refers to emerging national interoperability standards including the GSB.

The notice describes the Municipal Property Tax System as integrating with the councils' PFM Smart accounting software through the X-Road platform, first deployed in Kenema City Council as a pilot, with rollout to Bo and Koidu and then all 22 councils intended.

note: The announcement says the DEL is 'set to be' the linchpin and describes the data sharing layer 'once established'; it states no procurement, build or pilot, so no platform fact is recorded.
The document states nothing on this study's aspects for this country that the study's questions ask.
ASYCUDA is a single customs system with bank-teller validation; no government data exchange platform stated.
The Government Service Bus is named as the thing the roadmap will govern; its build or service status is not stated.
